q: The Indirect Taxes Enquiry Committee (1976), which recommended the introduction of value added tax at the manufacturing stage in India, was chaired by:
e: The Indirect Taxes Enquiry Committee of 1976, chaired by L. K. Jha, recommended value added tax at the manufacturing stage, which led to MODVAT.

q: The Committee on Industrial Sickness and Corporate Restructuring (1993), appointed by the Government of India, was chaired by:
e: The Committee on Industrial Sickness and Corporate Restructuring of 1993, which addressed sick industrial companies, was chaired by Onkar Goswami.

q: Harare is the capital of:
e: Harare is the capital of Zimbabwe, the southern African country formerly known as Rhodesia.

q: Windhoek is the capital of:
e: Windhoek is the capital of Namibia, the south-west African country that gained independence from South Africa in 1990.

q: Antananarivo is the capital of:
e: Antananarivo is the capital of Madagascar, the large island nation in the Indian Ocean off south-east Africa.

q: The 'Ngultrum' is the currency of:
e: The ngultrum is the currency of Bhutan; it is pegged at par with the Indian rupee, which also circulates in Bhutan.

q: The 'Dirham' is the currency of:
e: The dirham is the currency of the United Arab Emirates, issued by its central bank since 1973, replacing the currencies used by the emirates.

q: The 'Shekel' is the currency of:
e: The shekel, formally the new Israeli shekel, is the currency of Israel, introduced in 1985 to replace the old shekel.

q: The 'Hryvnia' is the currency of:
e: The hryvnia is the currency of Ukraine, introduced in 1996 after the country became independent from the Soviet Union.

q: The 'Koruna' is the currency of:
e: The koruna (crown) is the currency of the Czech Republic; Slovakia, which once shared it, switched to the euro in 2009.

q: United Nations Day is observed every year on:
e: United Nations Day is observed on 24 October, the day in 1945 when the UN Charter came into force.

q: World Diabetes Day is observed every year on:
e: World Diabetes Day is observed on 14 November, the birthday of Frederick Banting, co-discoverer of insulin.

q: World Tourism Day is observed every year on:
e: World Tourism Day is observed on 27 September, marking the anniversary of the adoption of the UNWTO statutes in 1970.

q: The Secretariat of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) is located at:
e: The SAARC Secretariat is located at Kathmandu, Nepal, from where the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation is administered.

q: The longest freshwater lake in the world is:
e: Lake Tanganyika in Africa, about 673 km long, is the longest freshwater lake in the world; Lake Superior is the largest by surface area.

q: The largest lake of Africa is:
e: Lake Victoria, shared by Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania, is the largest lake in Africa by surface area.

q: The Mariana Trench, containing the deepest known point of the world's oceans, is located in the:
e: The Mariana Trench, containing Challenger Deep, the deepest known oceanic point, lies in the western Pacific Ocean east of the Mariana Islands.

q: The Mojave Desert is located in the:
e: The Mojave Desert is located in the south-western United States of America, mainly in California, with parts in Nevada, Arizona and Utah.

q: The largest mangrove forest in the world is the:
e: The Sundarbans, in the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta in India and Bangladesh, form the largest mangrove forest in the world.

q: Who among the following is regarded as the 'Father of Microbiology'?
e: Louis Pasteur is regarded as the Father of Microbiology for his germ theory work, pasteurisation and vaccines, building the science of microbes.

q: The Hyderabad Metro Rail project, executed under the public-private partnership mode, has been built and is operated by the concessionaire:
e: The Hyderabad Metro was built and is operated under PPP by L and T Metro Rail (Hyderabad) Limited, the concessionaire for the project.

q: The Uttar Pradesh Metro Rail Corporation Limited (UPMRC), which executes the metro rail projects in Uttar Pradesh, is a joint venture of:

options.A: The Government of India and the Government of NCT of Delhi
options.B: The Government of Uttar Pradesh and the Lucknow Development Authority
options.C: The Government of India and the Government of Uttar Pradesh with equal equity participation
options.D: The Ministry of Railways and the Government of Uttar Pradesh

e: UPMRC is a joint venture of the Government of India and the Government of Uttar Pradesh with equal, 50:50, equity participation.

q: The office of the Chief Commissioner of Railway Safety, who heads the Commission of Railway Safety organisation, is located at:
e: The office of the Chief Commissioner of Railway Safety, who heads the Commission of Railway Safety under the civil aviation ministry, is located at Lucknow.

q: The Railway Staff College, now functioning as the National Academy of Indian Railways at Vadodara, was originally set up in the year 1930 at:
e: The Railway Staff College, now the National Academy of Indian Railways at Vadodara, was originally set up in 1930 at Dehradun.

q: The Zonal Railway Users' Consultative Committee (ZRUCC) of a zonal railway is chaired by the:

options.A: General Manager of the zonal railway

e: The Zonal Railway Users' Consultative Committee of a zonal railway is chaired by the General Manager of that zonal railway.

q: The cost of the Government Railway Police (GRP), which looks after law and order on railway premises and in trains, is shared between the Railways and the State Governments in the manner that it is:

options.B: Borne entirely by the State Governments
options.C: Shared equally (50:50) between the Railways and the State Governments
options.D: Shared in the ratio of 75:25 between the Railways and the State Governments

e: The cost of the Government Railway Police is shared equally, 50:50, between the Railways and the State Governments concerned.

q: The Chancellor of the Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya at Vadodara, the university set up for the transport and logistics sector, is the:

options.C: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Railway Board

e: The Minister of Railways is the Chancellor of the Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya at Vadodara, the central university for the transport and logistics sector.

q: The first Managing Director of the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation Limited (DMRC), who headed the corporation from its initial years and built the first phases of the Delhi Metro, was:
e: E. Sreedharan was the first Managing Director of DMRC and headed it through the building of the first phases of the Delhi Metro.

q: After the restructuring of the Railway Board in 2020, the train operations and business development functions in the Board are headed by the:
e: After the 2020 Railway Board restructuring, train operations and business development are headed by the Member (Operations and Business Development).

q: Under the Railway Claims Tribunal Act, the Chairman of the Railway Claims Tribunal is appointed from among persons who are, or have been:

options.A: A Judge of a High Court
options.B: A Member of the Railway Board
options.C: A General Manager of a zonal railway

e: Under the Railway Claims Tribunal Act, the Chairman of the Tribunal is appointed from persons who are or have been a Judge of a High Court.

q: The Uttar Pradesh Metro Rail Corporation Limited (UPMRC) was earlier known by the name:
e: UPMRC was earlier known as the Lucknow Metro Rail Corporation Limited, renamed when its mandate was extended to metro projects across Uttar Pradesh.

q: The Rail Coach Factory at Kapurthala, the second coach-building production unit of Indian Railways, was set up in the year:
e: The Rail Coach Factory at Kapurthala, Indian Railways' second coach-building unit after ICF, was set up in 1985.

q: The head of the Integral Coach Factory at Chennai, a production unit of Indian Railways, holds the designation of:
e: The Integral Coach Factory at Chennai is headed by a General Manager, as production units of Indian Railways are headed by General Managers.

q: The secretariat work of the Railway Board's office in the Ministry of Railways is mainly handled by the officers of the service known as the:
e: Secretariat work in the Railway Board office is mainly handled by officers of the Railway Board Secretariat Service, a dedicated organised service.

q: The B. R. Singh Hospital at Sealdah in Kolkata is the headquarters hospital of which zonal railway?
e: The B. R. Singh Hospital at Sealdah, Kolkata, is the headquarters hospital of Eastern Railway, whose headquarters are also in Kolkata.

q: The Railway Central Hospital at Garden Reach in Kolkata is the headquarters hospital of which zonal railway?
e: The Railway Central Hospital at Garden Reach, Kolkata, is the headquarters hospital of South Eastern Railway, headquartered at Garden Reach.

q: The Lalit Narayan Mishra Railway Hospital at Gorakhpur is the headquarters hospital of which zonal railway?
e: The Lalit Narayan Mishra Railway Hospital at Gorakhpur is the headquarters hospital of North Eastern Railway, whose headquarters are at Gorakhpur.

q: The Central Hospital at Lallaguda in Secunderabad is the headquarters hospital of which zonal railway?
e: The Central Hospital at Lallaguda, Secunderabad, is the headquarters hospital of South Central Railway, headquartered at Secunderabad.

q: The Central Hospital at Maligaon in Guwahati is the headquarters hospital of which zonal railway?
e: The Central Hospital at Maligaon, Guwahati, is the headquarters hospital of Northeast Frontier Railway, whose headquarters are at Maligaon.

q: The Central Hospital at Mancheswar in Bhubaneswar is the headquarters hospital of which zonal railway?
e: The Central Hospital at Mancheswar, Bhubaneswar, is the headquarters hospital of East Coast Railway, headquartered at Bhubaneswar.

q: The Central Hospital at Jaipur is the headquarters hospital of which zonal railway?
e: The Central Hospital at Jaipur is the headquarters hospital of North Western Railway, whose headquarters are at Jaipur.

q: The Metro Railway, Kolkata was given the status of a separate zone of Indian Railways in the year:
e: Metro Railway, Kolkata, the first metro in India, was given the status of a separate zone of Indian Railways in 2010.

q: The Kasturba Gandhi Hospital at Chittaranjan in West Bengal is the hospital of which production unit of Indian Railways?
e: The Kasturba Gandhi Hospital at Chittaranjan serves the Chittaranjan Locomotive Works township and is the hospital of that production unit.

q: The Central Hospital at Jabalpur in Madhya Pradesh is the headquarters hospital of which zonal railway?
e: The Central Hospital at Jabalpur is the headquarters hospital of West Central Railway, whose headquarters are at Jabalpur.

q: In Indian Railways, 'DEMU', the diesel-powered self-propelled multiple unit train services run on non-electrified sections, stands for:
e: DEMU stands for Diesel Electric Multiple Unit, the diesel-powered self-propelled multiple unit trains used on non-electrified sections.

q: In Indian Railways, 'CORE', the organisation executing railway electrification projects, stands for:
e: CORE stands for Central Organisation for Railway Electrification, the organisation that executes railway electrification projects, based at Prayagraj.

q: In Indian Railways, the designation 'DRM', borne by the head of a railway division, stands for:
e: DRM stands for Divisional Railway Manager, the head of a railway division, who coordinates all branches within the division.

q: In the divisional organisation of Indian Railways, the designation 'Sr. DPO', borne by the head of the personnel branch of a division, stands for:
e: Sr. DPO expands to Senior Divisional Personnel Officer, the head of the personnel branch of a railway division.

q: In the divisional organisation of Indian Railways, the designation 'Sr. DSO', borne by the head of the safety branch of a division, stands for:
e: Sr. DSO expands to Senior Divisional Safety Officer, the head of the safety branch of a railway division.

q: In the divisional accounts organisation of Indian Railways, the designation 'DFM' stands for:
e: In divisional accounts, DFM stands for Divisional Finance Manager, the head of the finance and accounts branch of a railway division.

q: In the hierarchy of the organised Group 'A' services of Indian Railways, 'HAG' stands for:
e: HAG stands for Higher Administrative Grade, a senior grade above Selection Grade in the Group A hierarchy of Indian Railways.

q: In the hierarchy of the organised Group 'A' services of Indian Railways, 'JAG' stands for:
e: JAG stands for Junior Administrative Grade, the grade officers reach after Selection Grade in the Group A service hierarchy.

q: In railway labour relations, 'NFIR', one of the recognised federations of railway employees, stands for:
e: NFIR stands for National Federation of Indian Railwaymen, one of the two recognised federations of railway employees.

q: In departmental selections of railway employees, 'GDCE' stands for:
e: GDCE stands for General Departmental Competitive Examination, through which eligible serving employees compete for higher posts.

q: In the track-monitoring organisation of Indian Railways, the special vehicle 'TRC', run to record track parameters, stands for:
e: TRC stands for Track Recording Car, the special vehicle run over lines to record track geometry and other track parameters.

q: The 'Him Darshan Express', introduced in December 2019 as the first Vistadome train service on the UNESCO-listed Kalka-Shimla line, runs between Kalka and:
e: The Him Darshan Express runs on the Kalka-Shimla narrow gauge line, so its other terminus after Kalka is Shimla.

q: The Ekta Nagar (Kevadia) railway station in Gujarat, inaugurated in January 2021 to serve the Statue of Unity, is recognised as the first railway station in India to receive which of the following?
e: Ekta Nagar station was the first railway station in India to receive Green Building certification for its eco-friendly design.

q: Which railway station at Jaipur became, in February 2018, the first station in Rajasthan and the second in India to be managed entirely by women staff?
e: Gandhinagar station in Jaipur became an all-women managed station in February 2018, the first in Rajasthan and second in India.

q: The Agartala Rajdhani, the first Rajdhani Express service of Tripura flagged off in October 2017, connects Agartala with which terminal?
e: The Agartala Rajdhani connects Agartala with Anand Vihar Terminal in Delhi, giving Tripura its first Rajdhani service.

q: Shokhuvi, which received its first passenger train service in October 2022 as the second railway station of its State, is located in the State of:
e: Shokhuvi is in Nagaland; it became the state's second railway station when passenger services began there in October 2022.

q: In June 2020, Indian Railways ran the world's first double-stack container train under high-rise overhead equipment on the electrified section of the:
e: The first double-stack container train under high-rise overhead equipment ran on the electrified Western Dedicated Freight Corridor.

q: Khongsang, which was connected by the first passenger train service of its State in January 2022, is located in the State of:
e: Khongsang is in Manipur; the first passenger train service to it in January 2022 linked the state through this station.

q: The Jhansi Junction railway station of Uttar Pradesh has been renamed as the:
e: Jhansi Junction was renamed Veerangana Lakshmibai Railway Station, after Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi.

q: The first Shatabdi Express service of the North-Eastern region, introduced in May 2017, was run between Guwahati and:
e: The North-East's first Shatabdi Express, introduced in May 2017, ran between Guwahati and New Jalpaiguri.

q: The redeveloped Gomti Nagar railway station, inaugurated in February 2024 and regarded as the first station redeveloped under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme to be inaugurated, is located in the city of:
e: The redeveloped Gomti Nagar station inaugurated in February 2024 is located in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh.

q: The 'Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri', the memoirs in which the emperor recorded the events of his own reign, was written by:
e: Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri is the autobiographical memoir of Emperor Jahangir, recording the events of his own reign.

q: The novel 'Tom Jones' (1749), regarded as one of the earliest and finest novels in English literature, was written by:
e: Tom Jones (1749) was written by Henry Fielding and is regarded as one of the earliest masterpieces of the English novel.

q: The science-fiction novel 'The War of the Worlds' (1898), describing an invasion of the Earth by Martians, was written by:
e: The War of the Worlds (1898), about a Martian invasion of Earth, was written by H. G. Wells.

q: The novel 'Sons and Lovers' (1913), centred on Paul Morel and his close bond with his mother, was written by:
e: Sons and Lovers (1913), centred on Paul Morel and his mother, was written by D. H. Lawrence.

q: The novel 'The Sound and the Fury' (1929), centred on the decline of the Compson family of the American South, was written by:
e: The Sound and the Fury (1929), on the decline of the Compson family, was written by William Faulkner.

q: The novel 'The Room on the Roof' (1956), centred on the orphaned Anglo-Indian boy Rusty in Dehradun, was written by:
e: The Room on the Roof (1956), about the Anglo-Indian boy Rusty in Dehradun, was Ruskin Bond's first novel.

q: The Malgudi novel 'The Financial Expert' (1952), centred on the money-lender Margayya and his rise and fall, was written by:
e: The Financial Expert (1952), about money-lender Margayya of Malgudi, was written by R. K. Narayan.

q: The celebrated Hindi novel 'Aadha Gaon' (1966), depicting life in the village of Gangauli in eastern Uttar Pradesh, was written by:
e: Aadha Gaon (1966), depicting life in Gangauli village, was written by Rahi Masoom Raza.

q: The celebrated Hindi novel 'Gunahon Ka Devta' (1949), centred on the love of Chander and Sudha, was written by:
e: Gunahon Ka Devta (1949), the Chander-Sudha love story, was written by Dharamvir Bharati.

q: The work 'Pariksha Guru' (1882), generally regarded as the first original novel in Hindi, was written by:
e: Pariksha Guru (1882), regarded as the first original Hindi novel, was written by Lala Srinivas Das.

q: The celebrated Bengali novel 'Chokher Bali' (1903), centred on the young widow Binodini, was written by:
e: Chokher Bali (1903), centred on the widow Binodini, was written by Rabindranath Tagore.

q: The celebrated Marathi autobiographical work 'Shyamchi Aai' (1935), a moving account of the author's mother, was written by:
e: Shyamchi Aai (1935), the autobiographical tribute to his mother, was written by Sane Guruji.

q: The celebrated Kannada novel 'Vamshavruksha' (1965), centred on the child-widow Nagalakshmi and the question of lineage, was written by:
e: Vamshavruksha (1965), centred on child-widow Nagalakshmi, was written by Kannada novelist S. L. Bhyrappa.

q: The celebrated Urdu novel 'Umrao Jaan Ada' (1899), centred on the life of a courtesan of Lucknow, was written by:
e: Umrao Jaan Ada (1899), about a Lucknow courtesan, was written by Mirza Hadi Ruswa.

q: The comedy play 'The Importance of Being Earnest' (1895), famous for its witty dialogue and mistaken identities, was written by:
e: The Importance of Being Earnest (1895), the witty comedy of mistaken identities, was written by Oscar Wilde.

q: The tragedy 'King Lear', centred on the ageing king who divides his kingdom among his three daughters, was written by:
e: King Lear, in which the ageing king divides his kingdom among three daughters, is a tragedy by William Shakespeare.

q: The play 'A Streetcar Named Desire' (1947), centred on Blanche DuBois and Stanley Kowalski in New Orleans, was written by:
e: A Streetcar Named Desire (1947), about Blanche DuBois and Stanley Kowalski, was written by Tennessee Williams.

q: The play 'The Cherry Orchard' (1904), centred on the sale of the estate of Madame Ranevskaya, was written by:
e: The Cherry Orchard (1904), about the sale of Madame Ranevskaya's estate, was written by Anton Chekhov.

q: The Second Central Pay Commission, appointed in 1957 to examine the pay structure of Central Government employees, was chaired by:
e: The Second Central Pay Commission, appointed in 1957, was chaired by Justice Jagannath Das.

q: The Third Central Pay Commission, appointed in 1970, was chaired by:
e: The Third Central Pay Commission, appointed in 1970, was chaired by Justice Raghuber Dayal.

q: The Fourth Finance Commission of India, constituted in 1964, was chaired by:
e: The Fourth Finance Commission, constituted in 1964, was chaired by Dr. P. V. Rajamannar.

q: The Aitchison Commission (1886), appointed during the viceroyalty of Lord Dufferin, was set up to inquire into:

options.B: The organisation of the civil services in India
options.D: The system of education in India

e: The Aitchison Commission of 1886, under Lord Dufferin, inquired into the organisation of the civil services in India.

q: The Famine Commission appointed in 1900, after the famine of 1899-1900, was chaired by:
e: The Famine Commission of 1900, after the 1899-1900 famine, was chaired by Sir Antony MacDonnell.

q: The Monopolies Inquiry Commission, appointed by the Government of India in 1964, was set up to inquire into:

options.A: The working of public sector undertakings
options.C: The concentration of economic power and monopolistic trade practices

e: The Monopolies Inquiry Commission of 1964 inquired into concentration of economic power and monopolistic trade practices.

q: The Choksi Committee (1978), appointed by the Government of India, is associated with recommendations on the simplification and rationalisation of:
e: The Choksi Committee of 1978 recommended simplification and rationalisation of direct tax laws.

q: The Alagh Committee (1979), a task force set up by the Planning Commission under the chairmanship of Y. K. Alagh, is best known for its work on:

options.B: The estimation of poverty based on nutritional requirements and minimum needs

e: The Alagh Committee of 1979 estimated poverty using nutritional requirements and minimum needs as the basis.

q: The Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission (FSLRC), set up by the Government of India in 2011, was entrusted with the task of:

options.A: Reviewing and rewriting the laws governing the financial sector
options.B: Recommending a framework for data protection

e: The FSLRC, set up in 2011, was tasked with reviewing and rewriting the laws governing India's financial sector.

q: 'Pomology' is the branch of horticulture that deals with the study and cultivation of:
e: Pomology is the branch of horticulture dealing with the study and cultivation of fruit and fruit trees.

q: 'Oncology' is the branch of medical science that deals with the study and treatment of:
e: Oncology is the branch of medicine dealing with the study and treatment of tumours and cancer.

q: The smallest country of the world in area is:
e: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world by area, smaller than Monaco, Nauru and San Marino.

q: The first Indian to swim across the English Channel, achieving the feat in 1958, was:
e: Mihir Sen was the first Indian to swim across the English Channel, achieving the feat in 1958.

q: Bharat Ratna Ustad Bismillah Khan, the legendary musician of Banaras, was a maestro of the:
e: Ustad Bismillah Khan of Banaras was India's legendary shehnai maestro, honoured with the Bharat Ratna.

q: Ustad Zakir Hussain, the celebrated Indian musician known worldwide, is a maestro of the:
e: Ustad Zakir Hussain is the world-renowned tabla maestro, the instrument for which he is celebrated.

q: The Elephanta Caves, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for their rock-cut sculptures, are located on an island near the city of:
e: The Elephanta Caves lie on an island in Mumbai harbour, near Mumbai, and are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

q: Which country is known as the 'Land of the Rising Sun'?
e: Japan is called the Land of the Rising Sun, as its name signifies the sun's origin in the east.
